meta.how_to_verify: sha256 of json.dumps({mission, time, region}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))

mission.name: Griffin Mission One (Astrobotic, CLPS)
announced: Launch on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy in the fourth quarter of 2026; no specific date announced (June 2026).
Scheduled for launch no earlier than November 2026.
Target: the Nobile crater region near Mons Mouton, at the lunar south pole.
Mission objective: a soft landing followed by at least five Earth days of surface operations.
assumptions: No landing point has been published. The time forecast uses the point where IM-2 Athena touched down on Mons Mouton (84.7906 S, 29.1957 E) as a stand-in; the region scan covers the wider Mons Mouton - Nobile area.
Trajectory not published: a direct transfer of 4 to 7 days into a 100 km near-polar orbit (80-100 deg), landing within 4 days of arrival, as tested on IM-1 and IM-2.

Landing rule as tested on IM-1 and IM-2: Sun 0.5 deg above the LOLA terrain horizon and rising, Earth 2 deg above it, plane change within 150 m/s; plus the announced five days of sunlight after touchdown.
TLI dates scanned from 1 November 2026 to 28 February 2027, so the forecast still holds if the launch slips.
Solar energy is the share of the solar disc above the terrain over one lunar day (14 days) after touchdown; panel orientation and efficiency are not modelled.
sources: Late 2026 launch, five days of surface operations
Mons Mouton coordinates; IM-2 touchdown point
NASA's VIPER site criteria: Earth visibility, illumination, slopes

grid.frame: LOLA south polar stereographic: x to the image right, y down

ranking.order: sunlight left by the best landing slot, then total slot time
